title: Continuous Feedback Processing
description: EEG dataset from twenty-one participants performing a continuous feedback learning task in which they predicted the final level of an animated rising bar. Cues (gnomes) differed in how predictable the outcome was (highly predictable, somewhat predictable, unpredictable), enabling study of feedback processing under varying outcome uncertainty. Points were awarded according to the accuracy of each guess.
methods_description: Each trial began with a fixation cross (400-600 ms), followed by a gnome cue (1500 ms) and a bar outline. Participants indicated their guess with the mouse. The bar then rose at 1 degree per second and the final outcome was shown for 1000 ms. Six gnome types defined the outcome distributions, and event triggers marked each trial stage. Participant 11 was excluded due to excessive artifacts.
